{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

ANTHONY'S CLARIFICATION, 2026-07-30, and it corrects the framing this node was first written with: what he wants committed is NOT the realized product or a future codebase. It is a SLICE OF THE REFLOW2 GRAPH ITSELF — "this is the planned capabilities of epoch_1, epoch_2 … epoch_n" — so that he can open the repo and see "that is when I get capability X", or "capability Y is not expected until increment_13". His words: "it isn't the realized product/artifact of the project, but snapshot of the project at epoch or increment that I'm looking to capture in git." He is explicitly open to something other than git.

THE FIRST FRAMING HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. This node originally organised everything around "git can only store the past, and a plan is not a past". That is too glib. A plan document is a PRESENT artifact describing a future, and committing one is ordinary — git stores plans perfectly well. The real objection was never to committing plans; it was only ever to using BRANCHES as the record, and that narrower objection stands.

(a) BRANCH PER EPOCH — `epoch_1`, `epoch_2`, each holding a projected design. Matches the mental model directly: check out `epoch_n`, look.
    Costs: checking out a branch normally makes the whole REPO reflect that state, and here there is no future code to reflect, so the branch buys nothing the file would not. A full export is 1.6 MB today, so N epochs is N × 1.6 MB of near-identical JSON, rewritten on every replan. Branches also invite merge semantics that do not apply — nobody merges epoch_2 into main. And the plan's MOVEMENT stays invisible: a branch pointer moves silently, which is exactly what `req:plans-move-honestly` needs to see.

(b) A FILE PER EPOCH ON MAIN — `docs/design/epochs/epoch_3.{md,json}`. Browsing is easier than a checkout, there is one history rather than N, and every replan is an ordinary commit to that file.
    THE PROPERTY THIS BUYS FOR FREE: `git log -p docs/design/epochs/epoch_3.md` IS the plan's revision history. A large part of `req:plans-move-honestly` — "when a planned epoch's content moves, the plan's own change is a dated event on the record" — would be satisfied by git doing what git is good at, rather than by new machinery in reflow2.

(c) RENDER IT, DO NOT AUTHOR IT — and this is what (b) should probably be generated BY. An epoch slice is a VIEWPOINT. `tools/render_views.py` already renders viewpoints as pure projections of the graph, already confesses anything a view needs that the graph cannot supply, and ALREADY RENDERS THE EPOCH CHAIN BACKWARD ("Axis Z as a viewpoint: the epoch chain, and what happened at each"). The forward direction is the same renderer reading scheduled edges instead of recorded ones. Under this option the graph holds the schedule as single source of truth, the renderer emits one small file per epoch, and git holds their history.
    Cost: a generated file can go stale against the graph — which is a drift check reflow2 already knows how to do, and the same one `dataflow.html` staleness already gets in another repo.

WHAT A SLICE ACTUALLY CONTAINS, since "slice" is the word he used and it is much smaller than an export: the epoch and its date, capabilities expected by then, requirements expected satisfied, KPPs required by then, the version combination pinned once it arrives, and the delta against the previous epoch. Kilobytes, not megabytes.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN IT WAS: not "git or not git", but WHICH JOB GIT DOES. Git looks right for the HISTORY of the plan document and for pinning arrived epochs; the graph looks right for the schedule itself. The failure mode to avoid is making git the source of truth for the schedule, because then two places disagree about when capability X arrives and neither is wrong.","name":"OPEN — how per-epoch slices of the design become browsable: branches, files, or a rendered viewpoint","rationale":"Anthony's idea, his clarification, and his invitation to suggest something better; recorded so the reasoning survives whichever way it goes.

Kept rather than tidied away: the original framing of this node ("git can only store the past") was mine and was misleading, and the correction is recorded rather than silently overwritten because the prior text is what a reader would otherwise have found and believed. The snapshot at `epoch:wire-planning-cluster` holds the earlier wording.

Not argued down: option (a) is his own original mechanism and is recorded with the mental model it serves stated first. Its costs are listed beside it, not in place of it.","status":"proposed"}
